questions.q: What must a class that implements an interface provide?
options: Nothing extra -- implementing is purely cosmetic
A body for every method declared in that interface
A static version of each interface method
Only the methods it chooses to use
questions.explain: To use an interface, another class must implement it by providing a body for all of the methods contained in the interface -- any class that implements an interface must define all the methods it declares.

questions.q: How many interfaces can a single Apex class implement at once?
options: Exactly one, same as extending a class
None -- Apex classes can't implement interfaces
More than one, separated by commas
Interfaces can only be implemented by other interfaces, not classes
questions.explain: A class can implement multiple interfaces, but can only extend one existing class -- this restriction is why Apex doesn't support multiple inheritance of classes.

questions.q: What access modifier do methods declared inside an interface have?
options: They must be declared private
They must be declared public explicitly
They have no access modifiers at all -- just a signature
They default to protected
questions.explain: Methods defined within an interface have no access modifiers and contain just their signature, with no body.

questions.q: What keyword declares that a class contains at least one method with a signature but no body, to be implemented by subclasses?
options: virtual
abstract
override
static
questions.explain: The abstract definition modifier declares that a class contains abstract methods -- methods that only have their signature declared and no body defined.

questions.q: Can an interface extend another interface in Apex?
options: No, interfaces can never extend anything
Yes -- an interface can extend another interface, giving the extending interface access to all of the parent interface's methods
Only if both interfaces are declared global
Only classes can use the extends keyword, never interfaces
questions.explain: Extensions also apply to interfaces -- an interface can extend another interface, and as with classes, all the methods and properties of the extended interface become available to the extending interface.
